label: Dribbble Jobs
terms_note: Design jobs; apply link to employer.

endpoints.call: keep — assist for apply; the public jobs RSS (application/rss+xml) is a usable public feed; the Dribbble API v2 is for publishing shots, not jobs
endpoints.notes: from the docs / live response read on 2026-09-05

reference.limits: Terms prohibit 'using any automated system, including without limitation robots, spiders, offline readers, etc., to access the Website … in a manner that sends more request messages to the Dribbble servers than a human can reasonably produce' and scraping / harvesting user data; Terms prohibit 'using any automated system, including without limitation robots, spiders, offline readers, etc., to access the Website … in a manner that sends more request messages to the Dribbble servers than a human can reasonably produce' and scraping / harvesting user data; robots.txt disallows /jobs/*/apply_now.

search.note: Dribbble Jobs RSS 2.0 feed (all current design jobs, ~50). keyword is the job board's search parameter carried into the feed (checked 2026-09-25: ?keyword=brand narrows the feed, a nonsense keyword returns an empty channel); location, page and limit are not sent (the feed is one list; ignore next_page). title is '<Company> is hiring for a position of <Role> in <Location>'; company is the dc:creator. id is the posting link.

not_offered.me: No credentials to verify ('auth: none'): the feed is public and has no account endpoint.
not_offered.get_posting: The feed has no per-item endpoint (each posting's url is an HTML page); search returns the whole record in raw.
not_offered.apply: No application endpoint: the feed only lists postings; candidates apply on each posting's url (employer page / e-mail).
not_offered.list_messages: No messaging API; the only machine-readable interface is the public job feed.
